Description: Format the card in the camera first so file numbering is contiguous

Optional: set the filename prefix to the group letter (A, B, C...) so you can see at a glance that a group is finished, instead of the usual month letter (H = August). Safe either way - the number keeps climbing across a prefix change, and the app takes only the digits as its sequence
RAW+JPEG for every frame unless the row says otherwise
Shoot the groups in order, leaving at least 10 seconds between lettered groups - longer is fine and makes the boundary clearer, so do not worry about hitting a number
Timing only matters where a row says back to back (B6, C2, D3) - those must be as fast as you can press. Everywhere else a bigger gap is harmless
Subject does not matter - point the camera at anything
Tell me any row the camera will not do, and the ART BKT selection you settle on in D2
Baseline - proves defaults are read as defaults, not as invented sequences
Sequential High burst - hold for about 10 frames
Two bursts of 4 frames, pressed back to back as fast as you can - the case the iPad over-merges today
Brackets that set the shot counter - tag 0x600
AE bracket 5 frames - two presses back to back
Focus bracket 6 frames at about 2 second shutter - the long-gap case that must not split
ART BKT with your current selection - one press
SETTING CHANGE: edit the ART BKT selection - drop two filters, add two others, and include both Grainy Film I and Grainy Film II
ART BKT with the new selection - two presses back to back
Partial Color - one frame, any wheel colour
Partial Color - one frame, a different wheel colour
Live ND at ND2 - one frame
Live ND at ND64 - one frame
Live GND at GND2 - one frame
Live GND at GND8 - one frame
Interval run - 10 frames at 3 second interval
One hand-shot frame within a second or two of F1 finishing
Second interval run - 5 frames, to show the counter restarting
Container coverage - the note sits in the JPEG APP1 segment but inside the ORF TIFF tree
Three frames JPEG only, RAW off
One frame at a smaller JPEG size or quality
Switch back to RAW+JPEG and shoot one frame
